correctness.rationale: Orthogonal conditional-expectation differences give a symmetric kernel with row masses 2^(-h-1) and 2^(-n). The exact row norm reduces to a one-dimensional binary Bellman recurrence. Its tent-shaped envelope is proved by induction for all real states in [0,1] and every finite horizon; the equality choices yield exactly two masks for n>=3. The companion exact-rational checker passed 14045 independent row, mask and recursion assertions; finite tests support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: An entire finite-depth dyadic multiscale family of 2^n orthogonal level projections is optimized exactly, with every optimizing mask classified. The norm grows linearly as n/3 while single-level and all-level choices remain uniformly bounded, providing a nontrivial stability consequence of scale decimation. This motivated complete extremal classification is not merely a renamed standard inequality.
